The need for reducing traffic from the local street system is also indicated by the high accident rates of the major intersections in the vicinity of the airport. A summary of high accident locations discloses that the intersections of Layton and Howell Avenues has been on the City of Milwaukee's number one accident intersection since 1971. This summary found on pages 69 % 70 also gives an indication that removing traffic from the local arterial system and putting it on the freeway system will reduce accidents significantly. The increased use of traffic signalization improvements leads to more localized traffic congestion. This results in a reduction in the level of service for thru traffic and that portion oriented to the airport.
The "no build" alternate is felt as not being realistic.

The State, County and City highway agencies must, in the performance of their duties, maintain the existing surface transportation systems in satisfactory conditions or, when traffic congestion warrants, upgrade or expand the transportation facilities to modern, safe, and adequate standards.
As an alternate to doing nothing, the local street and arterial highway network could be improved. The data from SEMRPC's traffic assignment analysis showed the effects on the arterial streets and highways with and without constructing the Airport Spur. These assignments show that there would be additional vehicle miles of travel, additional vehicle hours of travel, and a lower average operating speed on the regional transportation network without construction of the Airport Spur.
